name: Secretary of the Interior's designation of March 27, 1871 of a reserve for the Osage in Indian Territory
citation: Order of the Secretary of the Interior, March 27, 1871; confirmed by Act of June 5, 1872, 17 Stat. 228
promises: The Secretary of the Interior designated a reserve for the Osage in Indian Territory, a tract the Osage had selected; its boundaries were amended and confirmed by the Act of June 5, 1872 (Royce schedule).
today: In Osage Nation v. Irby (10th Cir. 2010) the court held that the reservation confirmed in 1872 had been disestablished; this went against the Nation.

openQuestions: A reservation grant, not a cession. Royce area 534 is the Osage reservation; this record and cession-1872-06-05-great-and-little-osage are the designation and the confirming Act for the same land.

The ICC title search for "osage" returned Dockets 9, 105-108 and 126; they concern the 1808, 1818 and 1825 cessions, an 1865 award with offsets, oil royalties paid to Osage County and attorney fees, not the Indian Territory reservation.
The Osage Nation's own account of the 1871-72 reservation was not located in this pass.

2026-11-08 sweep: Court of Claims and ICC full text searched for: Court of Claims names "osage" (66 Ct. Cl. 64 (1928) and 119 Ct. Cl. 592 (1951) concern the 1865 treaty lands in Kansas; 102 Ct. Cl. 545 (1944) concerns oil and gas taxes); ICC full text "Osage 1872". Kansas or Kaw Tribe v. United States, 80 Ct. Cl. 264 (1934), recites the 1883 Cherokee deed for this reservation and denies the Kaw a share in it; it makes no finding against the Osage. Nothing new.
